portsAndProtocols.purpose: Primary web access for end users and API clients.
Break-glass administrative access to production infrastructure; restricted to a named allow-list of source IPs.

securityControls.controlImplementationDescription: Account types (user, service, administrative) are defined and provisioned through the identity provider using role-based access templates. Account reviews are performed quarterly by system owners; disabled accounts are automatically removed after 35 days per the account-management standard operating procedure.

Organizational users are uniquely identified and authenticated via the corporate identity provider, which enforces multi-factor authentication for all interactive logins to the MSW administrative console and underlying infrastructure.
All cryptographic operations, including data-at-rest encryption and TLS termination, use FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules provided by the underlying IaaS platform's key management service.

The system is monitored continuously using host-based and network-based intrusion detection tools integrated with the centralized SIEM, with automated alerting for anomalous behavior indicative of attack.

Meridian implements a documented incident handling capability covering preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery, coordinated by the Security Operations team per the Incident Response Standard Operating Procedure.

parameterValues.parameterValue: annually, with continuous automated control monitoring for technical controls

securityControls.controlImplementationDescription: A continuous monitoring program is in place covering the majority of technical controls through automated configuration and vulnerability scanning. Manual/procedural controls are currently reviewed on an annual basis; automation of procedural-control monitoring is planned for FY27.

frrImplementation: Meridian maintains an automated asset inventory pipeline that queries the underlying IaaS platform's resource-tagging API every 4 hours to enumerate all compute, storage, and network resources within the MSW authorization boundary.
frrValidation: The inventory pipeline's output is reconciled weekly against the cloud provider's billing/usage export as an independent cross-check for untagged or orphaned resources.
frrAssessment: The independent assessor sampled the automated inventory against a manual resource enumeration during the FY26 annual assessment and found no discrepancies.

frrImplementation: Data flows between the MSW application tier, database tier, and the underlying IaaS platform are documented in the Certification Package Overview's information-flow repository, with each flow tagged with a security category of Moderate.
frrValidation: Flow documentation is regenerated automatically from network policy configuration (security groups / firewall rules) on every production deployment to prevent drift between documented and actual flows.
frrAssessment: Assessor confirmed via network configuration review that documented flows match observed traffic patterns during the FY26 annual assessment.

frrImplementation: The single third-party information resource in scope (the underlying IaaS platform) is identified in the Certification Package Overview along with its FedRAMP Certification status; the outbound-only email delivery dependency is documented as a non-certified third-party resource with a documented use-case justification.
frrValidation: Third-party resource list is reviewed quarterly by the compliance team against the current vendor inventory.
frrAssessment: Assessor verified the underlying IaaS platform's FedRAMP Certification status directly against the FedRAMP Marketplace during the FY26 annual assessment.

frrImplementation: Authenticated vulnerability scanning is performed monthly across 100% of the MSW authorization boundary, consistent with legacy Rev5 scanning cadence expectations, using an agent-based scanning tool integrated with the asset inventory pipeline.
frrValidation: Scan coverage is validated each month by reconciling scan results against the current asset inventory to identify any unscanned assets.
frrAssessment: Assessor reviewed 12 months of scan coverage reports during the FY26 annual assessment and confirmed consistent full-boundary monthly coverage with no unscanned assets identified.

frrImplementation: Meridian publishes an Ongoing Certification Report to the trust center every 3 months per the standard FRR cadence, summarizing certification data changes, accepted vulnerabilities, and reportable incidents for the period.
frrValidation: Report publication is tracked via an internal compliance calendar with automated reminders; a missed publication triggers an internal escalation.
frrAssessment: Assessor confirmed a consistent quarterly publication cadence by reviewing the trust center's report history for the trailing 12 months.

frrImplementation: Significant Change Notifications include, at minimum, a description of the change, its effective date, an assessment of impact to Rev5 Controls, and any affected third-party information resources, delivered via the trust center notification mechanism.
frrValidation: A sample Significant Change Notification is retained in the trust center's assessment-reports repository for reference.
frrAssessment: Assessor reviewed the most recent Significant Change Notification during the FY26 annual assessment and confirmed it contained all required elements.
